merger_name: National Dental Care – business assets comprising the Integrated Dental Health clinic, Katoomba, NSW

targets.name: The Trustee for Lottie Family Trust

party_page.name: The Trustee for Lottie Family Trust

merger_description:
NDC HoldCo Pty Ltd (together with its subsidiaries, **National Dental Care**), through its wholly-owned subsidiary, NDC Australia Pty Limited, proposes to acquire from the Trustee for Lottie Family Trust 100% of the business assets comprising the Integrated Dental Health clinic (**IDH**) (the **Acquisition**).

National Dental Care is a dental services organisation that operates a network of dental clinics that provide a range of general dentistry services. National Dental Care has dental clinics in all Australian states and territories, including New South Wales. National Dental Care is majority owned by funds managed by Crescent Capital Partners, an Australian private equity firm.

IDH is a dental clinic located in Katoomba, New South Wales, that provides a range of general dentistry services.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between National Dental Care
and IDH in the supply of general dental services in the local
area surrounding the IDH dental clinic
b. there are alternative suppliers of general dental services in
the local area surrounding the IDH dental clinic.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
